g.text: J2..J9 are bare 1.6 mm copper pads on the front (nothing to buy). NorthSec's original had 0.7 mm plated holes for the same eight points.

g.desc: J2..J9 are bare 1.6 mm copper pads on the front (nothing to buy). NorthSec's original had 0.7 mm plated holes for the same eight points.

g.text: The game: each LED circuit is open until the builder solders a jumper wire from any '+' pad to that LED's numbered pad. Cut a wire and its LED goes out.

g.desc: The game: each LED circuit is open until the builder solders a jumper wire from any '+' pad to that LED's numbered pad. Cut a wire and its LED goes out.

g.text: Pad 1 (J3) -> R1 -> D1 upper left, pad 2 (J7) -> R3 -> D3 upper right, pad 3 (J5) -> R2 -> D2 lower left, pad 4 (J9) -> R4 -> D4 lower right (front view), the pairing NorthSec used.

g.desc: Pad 1 (J3) -> R1 -> D1 upper left, pad 2 (J7) -> R3 -> D3 upper right, pad 3 (J5) -> R2 -> D2 lower left, pad 4 (J9) -> R4 -> D4 lower right (front view), the pairing NorthSec used.

g.text: A wire can only ever join VLOAD to a resistor, so no wiring mistake between these pads can short the supply or reach the coin cell.

g.desc: A wire can only ever join VLOAD to a resistor, so no wiring mistake between these pads can short the supply or reach the coin cell.

g.text: 1.3 k gives about 1 mA per red LED from the cell and about 1.2 mA from the badge (NorthSec used 330 ohm on 3.3 V, about 4 mA).

g.desc: 1.3 k gives about 1 mA per red LED from the cell and about 1.2 mA from the badge (NorthSec used 330 ohm on 3.3 V, about 4 mA).

g.text: SAO++ power select: the switch common (VLOAD) feeds the four '+' wire pads on the timer. Position 1 = badge 3.3 V, position 2 = OFF (pin 2 unconnected), position 3 = coin cell.

g.desc: SAO++ power select: the switch common (VLOAD) feeds the four '+' wire pads on the timer. Position 1 = badge 3.3 V, position 2 = OFF (pin 2 unconnected), position 3 = coin cell.

g.text: The badge supply and the coin cell sit on separate switch contacts and are never connected to each other.

g.desc: The badge supply and the coin cell sit on separate switch contacts and are never connected to each other.

g.text: LED-only board: SDA, SCL, GPIO1 and GPIO2 are not connected, so no series diode is needed on the cell (see docs/standard.md section 3).

g.desc: LED-only board: SDA, SCL, GPIO1 and GPIO2 are not connected, so no series diode is needed on the cell (see docs/standard.md section 3).
